Tiếng Anh có nhịp dựa trên trọng âm: các: English has a stress-timed rhythm: content words (nouns, main verbs, adjectives, adverbs, negatives, question words) are stressed, while function words (prepositions, articles, auxiliary verbs, pronouns, conjunctions) are usually said quickly and lightly with the vowel /ə/ – called the weak form. The gaps between stressed words tend to stay fairly even, so the weak words get “squeezed”.
